title: Best Meaco Dehumidifier (2026): Arete One, Arete Two, ABC & DD8L
dek: Britain's damp-home specialist makes some of the most thoughtfully designed dehumidifiers anywhere. Here's which Meaco to buy, and what to check before you do.
description: The best Meaco dehumidifiers, from the Arete One 12L and 20L to the Arete Two, MeacoDry ABC and DD8L Zambezi, plus what US buyers should check first.
intro: A **Meaco dehumidifier** is what many British households reach for when condensation, mold on window frames and indoor laundry drying collide every winter. Meaco is a long-established UK specialist that makes nothing but climate products, and its compressor and desiccant dehumidifiers are known for clean design, quiet running and thoughtful touches like dedicated laundry settings and built-in air purification.

If you're shopping in the UK or Europe, the choice mostly comes down to size and features. If you're in the US, there's an extra step: most Meaco models are built for 230-volt power and rated in liters per day under different test conditions than American units. We break down the current lineup, how to read Meaco's ratings, and when a US-market dehumidifier is the smarter buy.
topPicksLead: The **MeacoDry Arete One 20L** is the best Meaco dehumidifier for most homes: plenty of capacity for a whole flat or small house, plus a HEPA air-purifier mode.

products.whyWeLoveIt: The Arete One 20L is the model that made Meaco's name with a new generation of buyers. It combines a capable compressor dehumidifier with a HEPA filter you can run on its own as an air purifier, so it earns its floor space all year, not just in damp months.
products.performance: Its 20-liter rating is measured at 30°C and 80% humidity, the conditions UK brands typically quote. In real homes that translates to a unit that can keep a two- or three-bedroom flat in check through a wet winter, or dry a load of laundry indoors in a few hours. Owners consistently praise the clear display, the humidity readout and how quietly it runs on its lower setting.
products.notes: If you also want strong air purification in a US home, compare our [dehumidifier air purifier combo](/best/best-dehumidifier-air-purifier-combo/) picks, which are built for 120-volt outlets.

products.whyWeLoveIt: Not every home needs 20 liters a day. The 12L delivers the Arete One experience — tidy design, air purifier mode, easy controls — in a size that suits a bedroom, a studio or a one-bedroom flat.
products.performance: At 12 liters a day under UK test conditions, it's well matched to a single room or small flat with occasional condensation. Owners report it keeps [window condensation](/guides/dehumidifier-for-condensation-on-windows/) under control overnight and handles everyday humidity from cooking and showers. For persistent damp or frequent laundry drying, the 20L is the safer choice.

products.whyWeLoveIt: The Arete Two takes the proven Arete formula and refines it. If you're buying new and want Meaco's latest take on a combined dehumidifier and air purifier, it's the one to look at first.
products.performance: It shares the 20-liter class rating and HEPA purifier function, so the core drying performance is in the same league as the Arete One 20L. The case for the Arete Two is in the details — updated controls and design touches — rather than a big jump in water removal. Compare current listings carefully, because Meaco's feature sets differ between countries and production runs.

products.whyWeLoveIt: The ABC range strips Meaco down to the basics. If you need to deal with a damp bedroom or a condensation-prone box room and don't need a purifier, the 10L is an affordable way into the brand.
products.performance: At 10 liters a day under UK test conditions, it's a single-room machine. Owners like it for keeping a bedroom or small home office dry and for its straightforward controls. It's not the one for a cold garage or for drying a full family's laundry; for that, look at the 20L models or the desiccant DD8L.

products.whyWeLoveIt: Compressor dehumidifiers lose efficiency as rooms get cold. The DD8L uses a desiccant wheel instead, which keeps working in unheated garages, conservatories, garden offices and cold bedrooms where a compressor unit would struggle or ice up.
products.performance: It's rated in the 8-liter-per-day class, which sounds modest next to the 20L units, but desiccant models hold their output far better as temperatures fall. The trade-off is power: it draws more electricity than a compressor model would in a warm room. Owners in older, colder homes often say it's the only dehumidifier that made a real difference. Learn more in our [best desiccant dehumidifier](/best/best-desiccant-dehumidifier/) guide.

blocks.text: Those three numbers explain most of the confusion around Meaco in the US. A Meaco rating and an American pint rating are measured in very different air, so you can't convert one to the other with a calculator. And a 230-volt dehumidifier won't run properly on a 120-volt outlet, adapter or not. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) explains how US ratings work.

We don't lab-test. For this guide we compared Meaco's published capacity ratings and manuals across the current lineup, looked at which models suit which homes and climates, and read owner reviews in volume for recurring themes: noise, sensor accuracy, tank design, filter upkeep and long-term reliability.

We ranked models on how well they match common needs — whole-home damp, single-room condensation, cold spaces and laundry drying — and on whether the extra features of the premium models are worth paying for.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Meaco dehumidifier

items.label: Compressor or desiccant
items.text: Choose a compressor model (Arete, ABC) for heated homes and a desiccant model (DD8L) for cold, unheated rooms.

items.label: The right size
items.text: 10–12 liters for a single room or small flat; 20 liters for a whole flat, a small house or regular laundry drying.

items.label: Purifier mode
items.text: The Arete models double as HEPA air purifiers. Worth it if allergies or dust are a concern — see [dehumidifier vs. air purifier](/guides/dehumidifier-vs-air-purifier/).

items.label: Drainage
items.text: Check for a continuous-drain outlet if you want to avoid emptying the tank daily in wet weather.

items.label: Voltage for your country
items.text: Confirm the listing is for your local power supply. UK and EU versions are 230 volts.

A 20-liter compressor model in a closed room with the clothes airer nearby is the classic setup; in a cold utility room, the DD8L's gentle warmth helps. Our [best dehumidifier for drying clothes](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-drying-clothes/) guide covers technique and US-market picks.

sections.heading: Buying a Meaco dehumidifier in the US

blocks.text: Meaco's lineup is built and supported primarily for the UK and European markets. Before you order from a US address, check three things: that the model is a 120-volt North American version, that a US warranty and service path exists, and that replacement filters will be easy to get.

blocks.title: Don't use a plug adapter
blocks.text: A travel adapter changes the plug shape, not the voltage. Running a 230-volt dehumidifier on a 120-volt circuit can leave the compressor underpowered or damage it, and it will almost certainly void the warranty.

If a US-voltage Meaco isn't available, you can get similar strengths elsewhere. Fellow British brand Ebac sells US models (see our [best Ebac dehumidifier](/best/best-ebac-dehumidifier/) guide), and the Midea Cube line offers a similarly quiet, compact design with a lift-out tank. Our [best dehumidifier brands](/best/best-dehumidifier-brands/) roundup compares the field.

The **Arete One 20L** is the best Meaco dehumidifier for most homes, thanks to its capacity, quiet running and HEPA purifier mode. The **Arete One 12L** suits smaller spaces, the **Arete Two 20L** is the pick if you want Meaco's newest design, the **MeacoDry ABC 10L** is the budget way in, and the **DD8L Zambezi** is the answer for cold rooms. In the US, confirm voltage first — and if it's not right, choose a 120-volt alternative.

faqs.q: Is Meaco a good dehumidifier brand?
faqs.a: Yes. Meaco is a well-regarded British specialist known for quiet, well-designed compressor and desiccant dehumidifiers. Owners frequently praise its build quality, controls and customer support.

faqs.q: Meaco Arete One vs. Arete Two: which should I buy?
faqs.a: Both combine a 20-liter-class dehumidifier with a HEPA air purifier. The Arete One is the proven, usually less expensive choice; the Arete Two is the newer design with refined details. If price matters, the Arete One 20L is the better value.

faqs.q: Is the Meaco Arete One 12L big enough?
faqs.a: For a bedroom, studio or one-bedroom flat with typical condensation, yes. For a larger home, damp walls or frequent indoor laundry drying, choose the 20L.

faqs.q: What is the MeacoDry ABC dehumidifier?
faqs.a: The ABC is Meaco's simpler, more affordable compressor range. The 10L model suits single rooms; it skips the air-purifier mode of the Arete line.

faqs.q: Can I use a Meaco dehumidifier in the US?
faqs.a: Only if it's a 120-volt version built for North America. Standard UK and European Meaco models run on 230 volts and shouldn't be used with a simple plug adapter.

faqs.q: Is a Meaco desiccant dehumidifier better for a cold room?
faqs.a: Generally, yes. Desiccant models like the DD8L Zambezi keep removing moisture in cold, unheated spaces where compressor units lose efficiency, though they use more electricity in warm rooms.
